officials.name: Craig Roberts
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
officials.bio: Craig Roberts was born and raised in Clackamas County. He worked in law enforcement at the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office for over 40 years, serving as the elected Clackamas County Sheriff for 16 years. He was elected in November 2024 to serve as Clackamas County Commission Chair.

officials.name: Ben West
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
officials.bio: Ben West began as a Clackamas County Commissioner in 2023. Before entering office, he served as a City of Wilsonville Councilor from 2018-2022 and is a graduate level registered nurse. Ben is also the founder and executive director of the foster care organization Oregon Foster Families First.

officials.name: Diana Helm
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
officials.bio: Diana has been very active in local government and civil organizations, serving as Mayor of the former City of Damascus and as a City Council member. She has also served on numerous boards and committees, demonstrating her passion for public service. As a long-time small business owner, she brings a unique perspective on issues affecting businesses and economic growth in Clackamas County.

officials.name: Martha Schrader
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
officials.bio: Martha Schrader has served as a Clackamas County Commissioner since January 2013. She previously served as a commissioner from 2003 to 2009 (and during that time as Chair from 2005 to 2007). She took a brief break as commissioner and Martha represented Oregon’s 20th District as state senator from 2009 to 2011.

officials.name: Paul Savas
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
officials.bio: Paul Savas was elected to the Clackamas County Commission in November 2010. He has been involved in local government and civic organizations for years, and brings experience as the owner of a small business in Clackamas County for over 25 years.

officials.name: Catherine McMullen
officials.address: 1710 Red Soils Ct., Suite 100 Oregon City, OR 97045
officials.bio: Catherine McMullen began her service as County Clerk in 2023, overseeing the Elections, Recording, and Records Management divisions. She is dedicated to building public trust through good and responsive government, guided by values of accountability, transparency, and community inclusion.

officials.name: John Wentworth
officials.hours: Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: John Wentworth, the Clackamas County District Attorney, has served the community for two and a half decades. A Clackamas High School graduate, he returned home in 1999 after five years as a deputy district attorney in Coos County. With over 30 years of prosecution experience, John has built a reputation as a tough, fair and thoroughly prepared trial attorney.

officials.name: Kathleen Rastetter
officials.hours: Office Hours: Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Closed from noon to 1 p.m.) Phone Hours: Phones are answered by clerks Monday - Friday 9 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.

officials.name: Brian Nava
officials.address: Public Services Building, 2051 Kaen Road #460 Oregon City, OR 97045
officials.hours: Monday to Thursday 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: Brian Nava was elected as Clackamas County’s Treasurer in November of 2018. Brian brings over 20 years of government experience to the office. Prior to his election as County Treasurer, Brian was appointed as Clackamas County's first Internal Auditor in August 2015.

officials.name: Anthony Huacuja
officials.bio: Anthony Huacuja was elected to the Board of Commissioners in June 2024 to a term that ends December 2028. Huacuja represents District 2, which covers Gearhart and Clatsop Plains, and portions of Seaside and Warrenton.

officials.name: Courtney Bangs
officials.bio: Courtney Bangs was elected to the Board of Commissioners in May 2020 and re-elected in 2024, with her current term expiring December 2028. She began serving as Vice Chair of the Clatsop County Board of Commissioners in January 2023. Bangs represents District 4 and has a background in agriculture education, currently teaching at Encore Academy in Warrenton.

officials.name: Lianne Thompson
officials.bio: Lianne Thompson was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2014, reelected in 2018 and 2022 to a four-year term that expires in December 2026. She represents District 5, covering southern Clatsop County. A native of Michigan, Thompson holds a Bachelor's degree from Michigan State University and a Master's degree in social work from the University of Michigan.

officials.name: Mark Kujala
officials.bio: Mark Kujala was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2018 and reelected in 2022, representing District 1. A lifelong Clatsop County resident, he previously served 12 years on the Warrenton City Commission, including five years as mayor. He is currently the executive director of the Columbia Memorial Hospital Foundation.

officials.name: Pamela Wev
officials.bio: Pamela Wev was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2018 and reelected in 2022 to a four-year term that expires December 2026. She represents District 3, which covers most of incorporated Astoria. Wev owns Wev Consulting LLC, and has more than 40 years' experience in government service and consulting work in land-use and development.

officials.name: Tony DeBone
officials.bio: While living on Maui, Tony met his wife Kathy, a Central Oregonian. They married and had their son Michael in Hawaii, then moved to Seattle, Washington for four years where Tony worked as an Associate Computational Scientist doing drug discovery research. The family moved to Southern Deschutes County to seek a more rural lifestyle and to be closer to family. Prior to his job as Commissioner, Tony served on the Board of Directors of the La Pine Park and Recreation District as Board Chair and the La Pine Rodeo Association on Land Acquisition.

officials.name: Alan Zelenka
officials.bio: Alan Zelenka has lived in Eugene for nearly 30 years and serves the people of Ward 3 as a City Councilor. He focuses on environmental protection and sustainability, smart development and neighborhood protection, and fostering a fair and open city government.

officials.name: Greg Evans
officials.bio: Greg Evans is an Eugene City Councilor. He has a background as Associate Vice-President for Equity and Inclusion and Chief Diversity Officer at Lane Community College, and holds an M.Ed. from Oregon State University.

officials.name: Jennifer Yeh
officials.bio: Jennifer Yeh is a Eugene City Councilor serving from January 2023 to January 2027. She holds a B.A. in English and Psychology from the University of Oregon and has a professional background in museum coordination, administrative assistance, and higher education. Her key interests include citizen involvement, public safety, housing, transportation, and neighborhood livability.

officials.name: Lyndsie Leech
officials.bio: Lyndsie Leech is an Eugene City Councilor serving from January 2025 to January 2029. She has a background in public health and administration, having served as Executive Director for WellMama, Inc. and in various development roles for non-profits. Her community involvement includes the Territorial Parent Association and the Fern Ridge Community Action Network Board.

officials.name: Kaarin Knudson
officials.bio: Mayor Kaarin Knudson is an architect, writer, and educator with more than 25 years’ experience in design, sustainability, and community building. Trained as a journalist before becoming an architect, her work has always focused on people and place. In 2024, she was elected with 73% of the primary vote and 96% in the general election.

officials.name: Joel King
officials.bio: Joel King is the Ward 4 Representative on the City Council. He was sworn in on January 2, 2019, and his term ends on December 31, 2026.

officials.address: 101 NW A Street Grants Pass, OR 97526
officials.bio: Kathleen Krohn is the Ward 4 Representative for the City Council. She was sworn in on January 6, 2025, and her term ends on December 31, 2028.

officials.name: Seth Benham
officials.bio: Seth Benham is the Ward 3 Representative on the City Council, sworn in on March 3, 2025, with his term ending on December 31, 2026.

officials.name: Victoria Marshall
officials.address: 101 NW A Street Grants Pass, OR 97526
officials.bio: Victoria Marshall is the Ward 2 Representative for the City Council. She was sworn in on January 6, 2025, and her term ends on December 31, 2028.

officials.name: Rob Pell
officials.bio: Rob Pell is the Ward 1 Representative and Council President. He was sworn in on January 4, 2021, and his term ends on December 31, 2026.

officials.name: Rick Riker
officials.bio: Rick Riker is the Ward 2 Representative and Council Vice-President. He was sworn in on April 7, 2010, and his term ends on December 31, 2026.

officials.name: Casey Miller
officials.address: 225 W Olive Street Room 110 Newport, OR 97365
officials.bio: Casey has referred to himself as a generalist in regard to the various skillsets he brings to his work with the commission. Born in Newport, prior to his current term, Casey served our community as the Public Information Officer in the Board of Commissioners Office since 2008. As an elected official he brings 14 years of experience in communications, emergency response communications and unique administrative experience to his work as commissioner. Casey lives with wife, son and cat in just outside of Newport.

officials.name: Celinda (Cindy) Timmons
officials.bio: Commissioner Celinda (Cindy) Timmons, a 4th generation Umatilla County resident, grew up on a farm between Milton-Freewater and Umapine. A proud graduate of Mac-Hi, Cindy was heavily involved in 4-H, F.F.A. and other civic organizations - traditions carried on into adulthood. She is proud to share she is a farm girl at heart - learning how to drive using a 1957 Dodge Power Wagon and an Allis-Chalmers tractor.
